plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 8: Further Applications of Trigonometry
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single sketch on an unlabeled coordinate plane showing a position vector broken into its horizontal and vertical parts. Two thin axes with arrowheads at all four ends meet at the origin; neither axis carries a name or numbers, though a few short tick marks are spaced along them. An orange arrow runs from the origin up and to the right into the first quadrant and is labeled v = ai + bj, with v, i, and j set in bold. A dark blue arrow extends from the origin along the horizontal axis to the point lying directly beneath the orange arrow's tip and is labeled ai below the axis. A second dark blue arrow rises vertically from that point to the tip of the orange arrow and is labeled bj. The two blue arrows and the orange one enclose a right triangle whose legs are the components and whose hypotenuse is the vector. Drawing the components as arrows joined head to tail makes the vector read as their sum rather than as an abstract pair. The sketch supports the magnitude of v being sqrt(a^2 + b^2), read straight off the legs of the triangle.

interactionPlan.concept: A position vector v = ai + bj is the head-to-tail sum of its horizontal and vertical component arrows, and its magnitude sqrt(a^2 + b^2) is the hypotenuse of the right triangle those components form.
elements: horizontal and vertical axes meeting at the origin, arrowheads at all four ends, a few short tick marks, no axis names or numbers
orange arrow from the origin up and right into the first quadrant, labeled 'v = ai + bj' with v, i, j bold
dark blue horizontal arrow from the origin along the x-axis to directly beneath the tip of v, labeled 'ai' below
dark blue vertical arrow from that point up to the tip of v, labeled 'bj'
right triangle enclosed by the two blue component arrows (legs) and the orange vector (hypotenuse)
magnitude-triangle view: side lengths |a| and |b| on the legs, |v| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) labeling the hypotenuse, right-angle marker at the corner where ai and bj meet

interactions.label: a (horizontal component)
interactions.teaches: The horizontal component a controls only the length of the ai arrow and the sideways position of v's tip — the vertical part of the sum is untouched, so the components are independent

interactions.label: b (vertical component)
interactions.teaches: The vertical component b controls only the height of the bj arrow and the height of v's tip — the horizontal part of the sum is untouched, so each component shapes exactly one direction of the vector

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Seeing the component arrows as the legs of a right triangle makes the vector's magnitude a direct application of the Pythagorean theorem: |v| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2)

demo_steps.title: A vector as a sum of parts
demo_steps.narration: The orange vector v is drawn head-to-tail from its two blue component arrows: ai runs horizontally, bj runs vertically, and together they reach exactly the tip of v — that is what v = ai + bj means geometrically.

demo_steps.title: Independent components
demo_steps.narration: Drag the a slider: only the horizontal arrow and the sideways position of the tip change. Then drag b: only the height changes. Each component independently controls one direction of the vector.

demo_steps.title: The magnitude triangle
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the magnitude-triangle view: the components are the legs of a right triangle and v is the hypotenuse, so the Pythagorean theorem gives |v| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2). Watch the hypotenuse length update as a and b change.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A vector's components are the perpendicular legs of a right triangle whose hypotenuse is the vector itself — so adding components is head-to-tail arrow addition, and magnitude is just the Pythagorean theorem.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Unlabeled axes with arrowheads on all four ends and sparse tick marks, as in the textbook sketch. Orange v arrow from the origin into the first quadrant, roughly a 35-40 degree angle at defaults; bold serif math labels 'v = ai + bj' (v, i, j bold), 'ai' below the horizontal blue arrow, 'bj' beside the vertical blue arrow. Blue component arrows always arranged head-to-tail: ai along the axis, bj rising from its tip to the tip of v. In magnitude-triangle view, replace component labels with numeric side lengths |a|, |b|, label the hypotenuse '|v| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2)' with its live numeric value, and add a small right-angle square at the corner where the two blue arrows meet. Allow a and b to go slightly negative is not required — keep first quadrant; update all arrow geometry and labels live as sliders move.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for a: the learner changes the horizontal component, the ai arrow length and the endpoint of v move left or right, and the horizontal part of ai + bj is separated from the vertical part.
- Slider for b: the learner changes the vertical component, the bj arrow height and the endpoint of v move up or down, and the vertical part of the vector sum becomes visible.
- Toggle between components and magnitude triangle: the learner switches from labeled component arrows to a right-triangle view with side lengths and sqrt(a^2 + b^2), showing why the vector magnitude follows the Pythagorean theorem.

The magnitude of v = ai + bj is given as | v |= a 2 + b 2. See the figure.

Plot showing vectors in rectangular coordinates in terms of i and j. The position vector v (in orange) extends from the origin to some point (a,b) in Q1. The horizontal (ai) and vertical (bj) components are shown.
